articles.title: QVC Host Drops to the Floor After Awkward X-Rated Blunder
articles.description: Screengrab/QVC QVC host Toni Brattin was left mortified after an unfortunate gaffe while trying to sell a wig live on-air. During a broadcast on Wednesday, Brattin was displaying a “Salon Select Wig” to viewers while praising how it looks and feels. “It looks like you went and got a b---job at your–a blowout at your salon,” Brattin said before muttering under her breath, “oh my God,” and stifling laughter. Ever the professional, Brattin still tried to promote the wig after the blunder, but was overwhelmed by laughter. Co-host Terri Conn then had to take the reins and carry on with the show, with a mortified Brattin comically collapsing to the floor in embarrassment, which also promoted laughter from Conn. Speaking to TMZ after the incident went viral online, Brattin said she had no idea the camera was still on her when she fell to her knees. “It’s live television, and you know we all make mistakes,” Brattin said. “At that time I’m just hoping that the camera gets off me, but I can’t really see from behind me as I’m talking. I just want to get this shut down, and hopefully Terry saves my butt.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Terri Conn (@terriconnqvc) Read it at TMZ Read more at The Daily Beast.

articles.title: GTA 6 to Premiere Extended Look on Netflix - IGN Daily Fix
articles.description: In today's Daily Fix:Rockstar Games and Netflix are partnering for an extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6. The special will air on Thursday, August 27th at 12pm Pacific on the streaming service, followed by a debut on YouTube six hours later. In other news, an advisory sticker has been spotted on PlayStation 5 console boxes, warning consumers that Sony will eventually stop selling games on physical media. Despite immense pushback from diehard fans, Sony doesn't seem to be changing course on their plan for an all-digital future. And in related news, Capcom doesn't seem to be worried about physical media dying out. The developer/publisher reports that around 90% of its game sales come from digital, so their business will likely not be drastically affected by the end of games on disc.
